cases.title: One demonstration on the demo pair only, in plain words, Edit > Undo, no numbers

rubric.reason: Turn 3 calls speed_graph_demo on one pair, takes frames at 0.7 s and 1.3 s, and says "a short ease out of 0.5 s and a long ease into 1.5 s" with no influence numbers. It also points at the peak ("the peak has moved toward the start") and gives **Edit > Undo**.

Turn 3 reports one change in plain words with real names ("I've shaped Title's Position from 0.5 to 1.5 s") and gives Edit > Undo. It uses no field names or undo label and hands back the rest without offering more ("The other three are yours").

Every name and time comes from the snapshot or demo result: Title's Position 0.5–1.5, 1.5–3 and 3–4.37 s, Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position and Glow's Blurriness. The easing lesson on Title is backed by eased_layers.

Each turn is short and ends with something to do. Turn 1 asks about landing hard and turn 2 asks where the move is fastest. The turn 3 demo shows one change with undo and the peak, then ends "The other three are yours. Say done when you've shaped them." without a second walk-through.

Turn 3 shapes only Title's Position 0.5–1.5 s, takes frames at 0.6 s and 1.4 s, says it 'eases out of 0.5 s briefly and eases into 1.5 s for much longer', gives Edit > Undo, and notes 'the peak of that move has shifted toward the start' with no influence numbers.
Turn 3 describes one change in plain words with real names, says 'Edit > Undo reverses it', and hands back the other three moves ('The other three moves are yours') without offering to do them.

Every name and time used (Title, Position 0.5–1.5/1.5–3/3–4.37 s, Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness) matches the snapshot output, and 'the layer you eased in the easing lesson' matches eased_layers in the record.

Each turn moves one step and ends with something to do: Turn 1 asks the land-hard question after the required leave-outs, Turn 2 asks the reading question, and Turn 3's demo ends with 'Say done when they're shaped' after naming the three moves left.

Turn 3 shapes only the demo pair (Title's Position, 0.5 to 1.5 s). It previews frames early and late in that pair (0.7 s and 1.3 s), says 'a short ease out of 0.5 s and a long ease into 1.5 s', gives Edit > Undo and points out that 'the peak has moved toward the start', with no influence numbers.

Turn 3 describes one change on Title's first Position move in plain words, says 'use Edit > Undo' without an undo label or field names, and hands the rest back ('The other three are yours') without offering to do them.

Every name and time the mentor uses appears in the snapshot: Title, Position 0.5–1.5/1.5–3/3–4.37 s, Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness and Mentor Practice; 4.37 is a direct rounding of 4.367.

Each turn is short and ends with something for the learner: Turn 1 asks about hard landings, Turn 2 asks where the move is fastest, and the Turn 3 demo adds only a one-clause definition of influence before handing back the other three pairs with 'say done when they're shaped', with no second walk-through or demo.
